threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still refer to the Overground as the 'train'. Locals know it's all about the 'Gospel Oak to Barking', not just getting from A to B.
Heard a guy on the 36 arguing over who gets the last chicken shop wing. Turns out they were friends; just a late-night ritual.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Sitting in the park, I watched a kid trade a Pokémon card for a falafel. That’s Neukölln—where cultures collide at lunch.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a bus shelter turned gallery—art exhibitions right where you wait for the M29. Only in Berlin, right?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a local would know to avoid the Civic Center Muni stop when the fog rolls in—it's like a ghost town, and the dogs on the tracks are just the cherry on top.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a Muni at Civic Center just as a dog decided it was playtime on the tracks. Every single passenger groaned in unison—classic SF chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Plaça del Sol but miss the charm of the smaller squares like Plaça de la Vila. Less noise, more local life.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their insistence on using a map app for every corner, even when the street signs are right in front of them.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube'. Everyone around here just says 'the Overground' and gives you a side-eye if you mention the District Line.
Caught a glimpse of a guy in an old bomber jacket singing to his reflection in the bus window. It was 2 AM and somehow the whole thing felt oddly poetic.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I heard a toddler on my block reciting verses from Rammstein while waiting for the bus. You know you’ve arrived when the nursery rhymes get heavy metal.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find spontaneous techno parties in an abandoned building, complete with makeshift bars and art installations. It's a vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they smirk at the tourists fumbling with their BART tickets, especially when the machines go down again.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy serenading a dog on the Muni during last week’s delays. Everyone was frowning, but the pup was living its best life. Typical SF!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just gaudí and nightlife, but the mornings are filled with locals grabbing xurros from hidden corners and kids playing in the plazas.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they order a 'café con leche' instead of just a 'café' – it’s a dead giveaway.
